THE BUSINESS QUESTION

Where do users drop out of the ecommerce journey, and how do acquisition, funnel, and product patterns compare?

From source data to analysis

  1. Transformed nested GA4 ecommerce events in BigQuery with dbt Core, separating staging, intermediate, and mart layers.
  2. Built three fact tables and five dimension tables, with data-quality tests to support reliable analysis.
  3. Developed acquisition, funnel, and product dashboards in Power BI, and integrated Vanna AI for natural-language SQL queries against curated marts.

What the analysis revealed

Approximately 72% of product views did not progress to add-to-cart, highlighting the largest bottleneck in the analyzed purchase funnel.

Acquisition, funnel, and product views make it possible to investigate the journey from multiple analytical perspectives.

Context & limitations

The drop-off is an observed funnel metric. It does not establish why visitors left, demonstrate a particular design problem, or prove that a change improved conversion.

This is a portfolio project. The figures describe the analyzed data and model outputs; they are not claims of client impact.
